Title: Allergy Problems?
Question: I am allergic to mostly dust and polline and my allergies get really bad in the spring time/summer (like now) only my right eye gets red and waters non stop. I have tried eye drops but all they do is sting, and my nose is runny too and i have medication something like rhinobusin. I have contacts so when this happens i have to take them out but my eye doesnt get any better. What can i do?
Answer: sadly, you need the drops - the sting is not constant it will go away. 


Options: See allergist and have skin test and then get immunotherapy shots; however, until the immune system is reversed you might not get results (remember the shots are just a mix of everything that makes you allergic)  so you need to take meds along with the weekly shots.

Stay in A/C area as much as possible.  If really bad the doctors will recommend wearing a mask outside (I haven't done that, thought)

After being outside, the moment you get inside, change your clothes and take a shower = you need to get all the stuff that makes you allergic away from you.

Ensure house is clean and no mildew.  Wash linens in hot, hot water. Cover pillow and mattress with anti-allergic covers.

My doctor told me that the  machines that are advertised on TV to clean the air, really don't work  that well - so for me not to waste my money on one.

As allergic as you are, you will not feel relief until the first HARD frost. Even Fall is a bad time for allergens.

If you like to do outdoor stuff, suggest that you check the weather report (on the computer is best - weather.com or whateverf you use) and see what the allergens are for that day - and time of day - try to avoid being out at the peak times, if possible.

If you can handle at home, there are 1st generation (i.e. meds that have been on sale and approved by FDA for a while that used to be prescription and are now over-the-counter) that will help - try them out. Give each a month at least == Claritin, Benadryl and others (ask pharmacist)

Use anti-allergic makeup (like Almay) Especiaally around eyes.

Some people claim that Honey of the bees in your area helps them. I haven't tried this but I asked the doctor and pharmacist and they said it didn't but if I wanted to try it, to go for it as honey is good on/in anything.

Do not, when tempted to do so, open your windows at home - all the allergens come in and stay in.  Sadly, this is just a fact.  If you have to, then realize that you will suffer.

The doctor can do several things to help you = this is how they are handling mine:


For eyes: doctor can prescribe two different ones - to use morning and before going to bed (ones that I've used that work are: optivar and elestat (one drop of each med in the a.m. and at night)

For nose: Flonase and Astelin (two puffs of each in A.M. and p.m)

Singulair or Clarinex or both - depends how bad it is for you 

Allerx-dose pack: one in a.m. and one in p.m.

For sinus headache: just advil (ibruprofen) or tylenol. But if it gets so bad that the sinus is infected (i.e. sinusitis or ethmoid disease) then you will need prednisone to releave the inflammation.

Oh by the way, if your eyes get puffy/red and you want some relief this helps me: ice pack over eyes for about 30 mins.  OR take some camomille tea bagas (that have been wet beforehand) put in the freezer on a plate and then put on eyes untl the bags are warm --- I put a bunch of them in the freezer. When frozen then I zip lock them and they are ready when I need them.  Also, you need several to ensure you can put on both eyes for at least 30 mins.  

.

Don't forget to check "hidden files" before running your search option. Once done, your results will definitely give you the requested hidden file even if you forgot its name. If not, it means the file is corrupted by some unknown virus, and there is little you can do to remedy the situation. Answer: The importance of empathy for moral socialisation was one of the reason for the development of the violence inhibition mechanism model of psychopathy.34 43 44 This model was also prompted by work suggesting that most social animals possess mechanisms for the control of aggression.45 46 They noted that submission cues displayed to a conspecific aggressor terminate attacksfor example, an aggressor dog will cease fighting if its opponent bares its throat. The violence inhibition mechanism (VIM) is considered to be a functionally similar mechanism in humans where sad facial affects (distress cues) function as a human submission response. At its simplest, the VIM is thought to be a system that when activated by distress cues, the sad and fearful expressions of others, results in increased autonomic activity, attention and activation of the brain stem threat response system (usually resulting in freezing).43 According to the model, moral socialisation occurs through the pairing of the activation of the mechanism by distress cues with representations of the acts which caused the distress cues (moral transgressionsfor example, one person hitting another).43 A process of classical conditioning results in these representations of moral transgressions becoming triggers for the mechanism. The appropriately developing child thus initially finds the pain of others' aversive and then, through socialisation, thoughts of acts that cause pain to others aversive also. \n\nBlair has proposed that psychopathic persons have had disruption to this system such that representations of acts that cause harm to others do not become triggers for the VIM.43 This is thought to occur because the signal to the learning system concerning emotionally aversive stimuli is mutedthat is, the unconditioned stimulus (US) signal is diminished, thus impairing the formation of US-conditioned stimulus (CS) associations. Certainly, the autonomic response of psychopathic persons to the aversive US of sad and fearful facial expressions is muted relative to controls.34 At the neural level, this has been attributed to dysfunction within the amygdala.23 47

Question: What rhymes with canvas?
Answer: How to go about finding good rhymes:

To get a "perfect rhyme" you would have to exactly match all the sounds from the accented vowel to the end of the word.  That is, any perfect rhyme would have to end with "-anvas" (at least in sound, if not in spelling).
http://www.bartleby.com/61/83/P0188300.html

In this case there is no such PERFECT rhyme (something that is much more often the case than people realize).  But you can do rather well at finding a "NEAR rhyme" by matching the VOWEL sounds of these syllables ('full assonance'), ending with the same consonant sound ('final consonance') [or perhaps something close] and matching, or coming as close as possible to matching the remaining consonants.   In ANY case, the ACCENT of the words must be the same (words ending with an accented "-ASS" will NOT work!)

For the 'near matching' pay attention to sounds that are likely to provide the closest matches:

* /m/ and /ng/ sounds are very close to the /n/ sound (all three are 'nasals'), /d/ and voice /th/ are also reasonably close
* the closest sounds to /v/ are /f/ /b/ an /p/  (all are labials --formed with the lips); /th/ is close (esp the voiced version as in 'there')
* for the final voiceless /s/ you might be able to use the related voiced /z/ sound or the /sh/ sound (these three s-sounds are called 'sibilants')

Adding an extra consonant sound, or deleting one, esp. from a cluster or consecutive sounds may also work.   So for instance, you might omit the n or v, or add an r after the combination.

Finally, for the vowels -- perfect matching is desirable, but sometimes you can use something very close.   Also be sure you pay attention to WHAT the vowel sounds really are, which is NOT the same as looking at the letters!      

In this case 
1)  the a of "can" is the short a of 'cat' ,etc. -- but note that following it with an r changes it to a different sound;  also, since this vowel has the accent, it is likely to be less forgiving of substitutes (such as a short e).
2)  the "a" in "vas" is the unaccented, 'swallowed', sometimes almost non-existent vowel-sound called "schewa" or "schwa" [since that e itself is an instance of the sound].  Short unaccented vowel-sounds like short i and the sound of 'uh' may work but are not identical.

Now which of the possibilities will work may depend on the exact context in which you are using it -- some rhyme-schemes and types of poetry demand very close matching, others are more forgiving (a limerick for instance).    In some poetic contexts you can even play a bit with the pronunciation to make it match better.  AND occasionally a dialectal pronunciation may allow a word to work or work better which otherwise wouldn't.


So, here are some ideas:

iambus
campus, Grampus

Candice
canthus, xanthous
Kansas
ankus
angus
anxious
chancrous
polyandrous
pangus

enchantress  (the final  short e is not a perfect match, but close)

'command us', 'stamp us' and other two-word combinations may work, though notice that the final vowel is a short u, not a schewa.  (Since the final word IS a separate word it takes more accent which prevents the vowel from being 'reduced' all the way to a schewa.) 

IF the dialect you use 'drops' final r's, the following might work:
ambers, cambers
camphors

Sometimes the following words virtually drop the middle syllable, which might make them reasonable matches:
amorous, clamorous, glamorous  (to indicate the shortened version one might write them as "am'rous", etc.)

Question: Why use a static IP address rather than a Dynamic?
Answer: In a corporate network, you want a Static IP for any servers or any computers hosting resources or providing any kind of service (web servers, printers, routers, file servers, etc). That's because a Dynamic IP does not guarantee a machine will keep the same IP all the time, and if a server/service provider changes IP, the clients may not be able to find it.  \n\nIt's the same for the Internet--- if people/web clients/whatever external computer will be coming to your computer to retrieve information or services, it has to be able to find the resource.  \n\nThis is usually facilitated by DNS which keeps track of server/service names and their corresponding IP's; DNS updates to client machines is sometimes slow, so the clients may go looking in the old location (old IP) if the server changes IP, and the DNS updates themselves may be done manually so the DNS server may not even be aware that your server has changed IP.

Title: What qualities make a great goaltender?
Question: Like Roy - what made him the greatest (IMO)?  Or Hasek or Brodeur or even Miller...?  Is it stance, leadership, size, "je ne se qua"...?
Answer: I think every goalie has his or her own winning combination -- some of them are brainy like Roy or Shields, some are huge and massive and forwards fear them like Brodeur, some are unbelievably quick and nimble and weirdly preternatural in a scary "spidey sense" way about the puck.  Nabby was that way for a while, Toskala now.

Like any other position, I think the best goalies reinvent the game at their level.  They own the plays, the net, their role on the team, and I don't think that necessarily amounts to leadership, but it does come from things like maturity and a certain solid footing.  Um, no pun intended.

I think some of the things I look for in a goalie I play with in rec are similar in pro hockey.  I don't like goalies who fall apart after letting one or two in, or goalies who are inflexible in their approach, which means they can only shut out certain teams and only if we defend a certain way in front of them.

I like playing with goalies who are fluid about the game, not prima donnas, who can clear their own crease if they have to and who can and will drive the game from the net if the situation warrants it.  Goaltending isn't for the fainthearted, and there's some wussy goalies out there.  I don't think, long term rec or pro, they do very well.

I was sad to see Shields go so completely downhill.  He was amazing to watch when he was at his best, and I wish he'd seen his full potential.  I'm watching Aebischer and Toskala now, of the new generation.  Then again, I know jack about goalies except for living with one.  

They have too much expensive gear and they leave it lying around all over the !@#!!! house.  That's my opinion on goalies.  How's that?  :p

It encodes video streams into standardized and compressed format while creating a video.
It also decodes video files from various compressed  formats to video streams while playing that video.
Downloaded videos are smaller in size for saving download time, so they are encoded/compressed and need certain kind of codecs to play.
Perhaps your machine doesn't have some of such codecs.
Do this: check the extension of the video you are trying to play.
It might ve .avi or .mp4 or .divx, install DivX codec pack.

And you can now play those video files.

Question: Should coal power continue to be used?
Answer: Well, currently all technologies have their drawback.  I'll go into detail what's up and why:

Nuclear fission - older LWR (light water reactors) are inefficient.  They use less and produce more waste as compared to the newer models using heavy water and sodium cooled reactors.  New generations of nuclear fuel are providing greater efficiencies.  I believe the best would had been the Integral Fast Reactor.  This would had provided proliferation resistant means of producing power.  Waste would had been sorted out with their pyroprocessing methods, and stuff that would be buried would have a half life of no more than 100 years.  It could use up LWR waste and other wastes from lesser efficient breeder reactors to produce power indefinitely.  It could convert at most 20% of waste back to fuel, and reuse.  But with the whole process, the waste leaving would be completely free of actinides and other long lasting radioactive materials.  So, nuclear fission would had been my favorite, if there wasn't such a public outcry for the source.  Until public opinion changes, there will not be any new sources in the US for a while.  Additionally, cost overruns of power plant production (because of a lot of safety mechanisms needed) would deter a lot of investors.

Natural Gas - you know gas.  It's gaining a foothold in the US.  Technologies are becoming more efficient and cleaner.

Nuclear Fusion - Something for the future, but until it's a proven technology, we can't live off of pipe dreams.

Coal - ah, coal.  It is the current favorite source of power in the US.  There are more advanced power plants called coal gasification power plants which uses scrubbers and other means of cleaning up the air.  This is slated to be replaced by natural gas by DOE's estimates.

Wind, Geothermal, and other sources - 
Wind requires expensive equipment that could alter the landscape.  Again, go check on the DOE's website, but they require many windmills to achieve what one powerplant can.  Geothermal requires hot sources in the earth.  Yosemite could be one, if it wasn't preserved.  Look at iceland for that. Solar is expensive and dependant of climate conditions.  It is better in the desert, but in cities with varying climates, we are dependant on a consistant power source.  Tidal sources of energy could be feasible if it didn't alter marine life ecosystems.  Currently it's a newer source of energy.  Scientists haven't perfected the technology to provide a competative means of power source.

My conclusion:
Yes I think coal should be continue to be used for the moment.  Currently, we cannot just change from one source to another because of current technologies and public perception.  There is a great market for this source of power - it won't dissapear in an instant until there are rivalling technologies that could provide comparable rates.  In the end, $$ are the deciding factor between the feasability of one source versus another.

Answer:

Answer: My great grandfather was Sicilian. He came over at the age of 12, because of the repression in Sicily. Sicilians were mostly farmers, vineyards and vegetables, but they were excellent builders. He caught on with a stone mason and became a master and at the age of 18 began building his own houses, in South Philadelphia, just north of where the Phillies and Eagles now have their stadiums, they are beautiful stone buildings with character and the craftsmanship has no peer. He also continued his winemaking and sold a few bottles on the side; especially during prohibition. Now you have to understand that they came from a very difficult situation, back home the local gangs would steal their crops and worse, so they formed an organization for self preservation called The Black Hand, which we know as the Mafia. Many of his friends came from this circumstance and learned at a young age to fight for everything, there were some very dangerous characters among them and I knew a few, of course we only knew of them as uncles and their business was never spoken of. Anyway, my grandfathers money was all tied up in his houses and when the depression came, he was ruined.  He went back to day work as a bricklayer, but of course there wasn't much building then. Title: Why can't we remember things that happen to us when we were babies?
Question: I vaguely remember that there are long term and short term memories. If there are emphasis on short term memories (e.g we think about it again), it might then be stored as long term memories. But why can't we remember anything from when we were very young?
Answer: Thats a very interesting question, and has been addressed at least to some point-It's clear, though we don't conciously remember events, that we do learn a great deal during this time, thus we "remember' a huge amount- the process of walking, controlling your limbs, facial expressions, on and on and on, are all learned and remembered event from infanthood- What we don't seem to remember are events per se- It appears as if that portion of our learning is developmentally controlled, such that the limbic system filters much of the detail out in infancy- only later, when high-level socialization occurs, does the limbic system start to recognize details and allow them to reach long-term memory. Essentially, the brain and learning are very very tightly developmentally controlled, so that certain things are learned at certain times- biologically, the brain is wired such that the most critical learning, such as how to control the body, how to interact in the most general way with people, etc, are learned first, and everything else is weeded out.  It's probably critical that this occurs, else we would remember being a baby at the expense of not learning how to walk until we were in Junior high!\nJust to address some things that were said before-we have an excellent memory as infants, and learn extremely quickly, but it is wired in a different way- There is also no evidence that events are stored at all, and thus no evidence that any of the infant memories can be "recovered" because they were not laid down to begin with.

Title: What is Zero?
Question: In a previous question, I asked what 0/0 is.
This question, apparently asked several time before, brought out many opinions or moderately and highly educated people, and I thank everyone for answering!!!

But now, let's wipe all that aside.  This is a brand new question.

I want to explore the nature of the number 0.

I would like to know what benefits and consequences would occur if we treated 0 as a non-reducible number equal to 1 divided by infinity and gave is a clever symbol, like z, much the same way we treat i equal to the square root of negative 1.

I beleive doing this could solve quite a few conundrums, including 0/0.

I beleive the key is redefining how we think of the number 0 and admitting that there is no such thing 0.

Comments?
Answer: 0 in modern algebra is the additive identity. Given a function + that assigns a number to a pair of numbers, 0 is the unique number such that +(0, a) = +(a, 0) = a for every number in the set. Without 0, most of the richness of modern mathematics and proofs would be buried in cases or would be quite impossible (There are many rings, groups, fields, vector spaces, monoids, and a menagerie of other algebraic structures around us). All these structures have some sort of identity element that provides an amazing amount of additional implied structure just by existing (An example you may be familiar with is calculus; it reduces nonlinear forms to linear vector fields at each point. The existence of the 0 linear map, studied in linear algebra, lends a plethora of structure to calculus, allowing us to find extrema, curvature, invariants, etc.). As linear algebra is also used extensively in the study of differential geometry/equations, modern physics is built around the properties of 0. It is the keystone in so many proofs that without it, they would either be irreducibly ugly or would not be true at all.

As to your definition of 1/infty being 0, many number systems that include infty also have 1/infty = 0. Such systems include the affinely extended real numbers and the compactification of the complex plane. These structures are very useful in complex analysis/topology. Neither of them are fields. See the sources for details.

Question: how were the catskills formed?
Answer: Geologists state that 200 million years ago a series of 'bucklings' caused by shifting tectonic plates created the Appalachian chain of mountains, which run from Tennessee across the Canadian Border. The Catskills are a portion of this plateau which simply "refused to go along." Their bedrock refused to "buckle". Instead this bedrock rose up by easy stages from the shallow sea in which its rocks (sedimentary?) had been formed (deposited?) from ancient mountains to the east. Raised high in the air the plateau became easy prey to the cutting action of the streams which carried off the plateau's rainwater. The plateau was carved up over 100's of thousands of years...the tough, hardest parts remained while the softer material was disposed of by various erosion techniques and actions including frost, water action and wind. Geologists explain the Catskills are simply a tough part of the Allegheny Plateau which the streams, even with the help of frost and gravity have not yet cut down to size. Over vast geologic time, of course, these forces will do away with the whole thing. In the meantime, scientifically speaking, the Catskills should be described as 'a maturely dissected part of the Allegheny Plateau".

Question: Why do we drop the "d" in the word "Wednesday" to make it sound like "Wensday" when pronounced ?
Answer: zberryfunk does a good job of explaining that way sounds in a word are naturally changed to ease pronunciation.  And some of the things he mentions may at least partly explain how we came to say "Wensday".

BUT  that doesn't entirely explain the spelling.    Nor even the pronunciation.   In fact, the written records show that it was all a bit messier than that.  Apparently the pronunciation varied through the centuries and from one dialect to another.  (And to this day there are some dialects in which the 'd' can still be heard.   Some of this is documented in the Oxford English Dictionary.) 

A couple of  obervations and suggestions:

1)  SPELLING
We retained the spelling with 'd' either because dialects that pronounced it were dominant (or at least 'won out' on this point) OR from the desire of teachers and grammarians to preserve some of the ROOT form of the word ("Wodens-die" and the like) even when it was no longer pronounced (something scholarly sorts have OFTEN done, at times even inserting unpronounced letters "back" into words they believed had come from a particular root).  OR maybe is was some of each.

But though the "d" won in the SPELLING fight,  "wensday" won the PRONUNCIATION battle.

2) PRONUNCIATION
 At least one of the written forms listed in the OED is wendesdei (from ca. 1275).   This inversion of letters (called "metathesis") to simplify the pronounciation is another common occurrence in spoken language.  Compare the word "comfortable" which is widely pronounced as "comfterbl" or even [losing the r entirely"comtubl"].     

Notice that these sorts of changes -- loss of middle sounds, esp. vowels (called "syncope" or "elision") and metathesis -- are very common  in the UN-accented syllables of longer words.

At any rate, a pronuciation "Wendesday" > "Wendsday" is very easy to understand.  And note that if you can scarcely hear a difference between "wends" and "wens".  That's because the d an z-sounding s are both voiced AND pronounced at the same point in the mouth.  [Cf. how "scents" and "sense" sound the same, despite the T in the first.]

Title: whats the deal with the male sea horse giing birth to his young?
Question: can you also give me an evolutionary aspect?  Do any other animals behave that way?
Answer: They only hold the eggs in a special sac, until they hatch.  (I think seahorses are egglayers.)  Once the young seahorses are ready to lead independent lives, he dumps them out of the sac.

I think it is comparable to the way male emus incubate the eggs of their partners.  Male emus (an Australian bird, similar to the ostrich and rhea) also cares for the young; they follow him, for a while after hatching.

See?  The females lay eggs / give birth, really.  These males just participate in care of their offspring.  Their babies are thus more likely to grow up and have offspring; the trait has selective advantages.

In general, females put a lot more into young than males do.  In some species, the way "female" is distinguished from "male" is by comparing the size of their gametes.  Note how sperm are smaller than ova, for example.  In many cases, the female adds a huge load of nutrients to the young, too; the yolk + / or white of the egg, the placental nutrition of the foetus, the milk of mammals...  It all weakens the females, in cases where nutrients are limiting (which is the normal situation, "in the wild".

In cases where males take on the bulk of after - care, it just evens the load a bit, really.  It lets the females get back to replenishing their body nutrients, to get ready for the next brood.... probably sired by the same male.  (He wins again.)

Title: Delphi Indy TCP Client / Server send recive Files using latest version 10. >?
Question: Hi, i am new to using Indy and is trying to create a simple client server chat program and need to add file transfer to it so fare no luck with it any demo/ advice would be appreiated thank
Answer: I've used the Indy 8 and 9.  The standard TIdTCPServer component should suffice to build a simple chat application.  The client application would use the TIdTCPClient component.  The most direct method is to work out some standard commands, and assign them to the server's CommandHandlers property.  It would also be useful to work out some standard response codes so the client knows what the server is doing.

When chat messages are sent (for example through a SendCmd call to TIdTCPClient), you simply have the CommandHandler on the server read the incoming text (OnCommand for the CommandHandler) the iterate the clients (TIdTCPServer.Bindings) and Write the text to the connections.  The clients can periodically call ReadLn (during a timer event) to check to see if the server sent any chat messages.

Things to keep in mind:
On the server, each client connects using it's own thread, so you have to have some familiarity with thread synchronization.

If you're planning to use the chat server over the Internet, you should have a cursory understanding of how firewalls work (e.g. port blocking) in case clients can't connect to your server.

Ultimately, there should be some examples in you Indy install directory or in your Delphi demos directory.

Enjoy!

Hope this helps.

Answer:

Thanks
Answer: I have recently implemented a photoserver running from my home computer.  I also have a dynamic IP address.  I used a free version of software from 'www.no-ip.com' to take care of my dynamic IP.  I was using tzo.com, but they raised their prices - free is even better.
Also, sometimes your ISP will block the default (incoming) port 21 for FTP.  Some free dynamic redirection providers allow you to have your FTP or Web server listen on any specified port - above what your ISP might be blocking.
For the FTP side of your question you could use Microsoft IIS (Internet Information Services), define an FTP server, select the same port as what you specified with your free dynamic IP account, ensure that your router doesn't block this port.
IIS can be challenging to use for an FTP server, you may want to look at Filezilla.
Hope this helps.

Answer: Not nearly enough facts. If your vehicle was executed against to satisfy a personal judgment against the other party, you could have filed to intervene in your friend's action and quash the execution on grounds that your property interests were being damaged. You could also have offerred to pay the reasonable value for your friend's interest in the vehicle in return for his/her relinquishing title. Then your payment could have been used to satisfy his/her debt to the creditor, and you would have clear sole title to the vehicle. \n\nGenerally, a creditor who executes against a vehicle held in joint title must post a bond in case the execution turns out to damage someone else's interests. Title: what are the activites done by farmers in rural area ??
Question: hint i want a good brief answer
Answer: Farming.

Small farms: everything.  The work literally never ends.  Tilling, planting, fertilizing, watering, harvesting, selling, repeat as many times per season as the climate and crops permit. 

In rural Utah, watering is the critical factor, as everything is run on irrigation systems.  People move pipe or repair pipe quite a bit.  For really small farms, they'll usually grow a few acres of alfalfa for their own animals and to share.  So, there are three or so crops a year of that, which includes bailing and stacking the hay.  

If the farm has animals, they come first.  Always.  My first job was working on a small horse ranch in Utah, where we'd first attend to the animals needs, then go paint a barn, repair a machine, cut thistle in the pasture, burn weeds in the irrigation ditches, or whatever else was pressing.

Large farms: they're more like corporations than old-style farming.  People would have jobs broken down, computers run and manage everything, planes do the fertilizing, the tractors automate much of the work.

Mixups in medical records can also cause them to recommend EFMP status. I was told I had Hodgkin's (cancer) when someone else's exam sheet was placed in my record by mistake. Best bet, work with the your physician to negate any faulty reasoning on the EFMP evaluators part. \n\nThe EFMP is required by DoD and then usually managed on an installation level. To find out if an appeals process is available ask the EFMP office or patient liaison for the SOP or LOI that covers EFMP processing.

Title: How are scientists considering creating a quantum computer?
Question: What are the techniques suggested in the process?
Answer: It will utilise quantum mechanics. At the subatomic level, matter behaves very differently to classical mechanics that we are familiar with in everyday life. The spin property of particles is not actually the particle spinning like a top, but is a term given to their angular momentum to help explain their interaction with each other.

Particles can only spin in certain allowable directions, electrons have only 2 directions, other particles can have more. The ability to be in 2 spin states at once is due to uncertainty in that the particle could be in either state until it is observed and probability functions are used to describe its state.

Similarly a particle in a quantum well (a box with walls of electric potential) will move about with its energy in a fashion that can be described by its wave function. At any measurement it will be in a certain point (although with unknown momentum) but it will vary with every measurement.

These sorts of uncertainties are what are scientists are hoping to use in quantum mechanics. Calculations will actually be performed millions of times simultaneously providing varying results, but favourable probabilities will lead to the correct answer with immeasurably small innaccurary.

Potential methods will utilise the spin magnetic moments of electrons, or the position of valence (outer) or free electrons moving between pairs of ions (charged atoms) accurately positioned in a semiconductor. There is still a lot of work required.

Question: I have a customer treating to sue me for adding her photo on a flyer I posted at grocery store bulletin. Answer: The law states that if you do creative work for money (i.e. for a client that pays you) they are the rightful owners of the copyright on that document.

The one place you can disply the photograph without permission is in your portfolio (provided you have one).

Question: Are there organizations prepared for other means of energy for  depletion of earth's combustable  resources?
Answer: I must disagree with gran. Most objections to the overpromotion of hydrogen have nothing to do with affluence or aversion to hiccups. Rather, the naysayers see hydrogen being touted as THE solution, with scant attention being paid to minor details like where the energy to generate hydrogen comes from. \nWith current technology, getting energy from hydrogen would merely be displaced combustion of fossil fuels or nuclear energy. It is either extracted from hydrogen bearing molecules like petroleum products or electrolyzed from water. Either way uses more energy than the combustion of hydrogen will repay, even in a relatively efficient fuel cell. Biological methods for hydrogen generation are being proposed but are unlikely to be economically scalable. Without a clean production technology, hydrogen is a net negative. However, hydrogen is intrinsically a clean fuel, and if clean production, transportation and storage can be arranged, it would improve our lives tremendously.\nOK, with that said, there are many organizations pursuing many alternative energy technologies. "Prepared" for oil depletion they are not. But they are working realistically along the many routes available to mitigate the shock of depletion. These include increased energy efficiency (note that the energy you don't use is equvalent to production of that energy with infinite efficiency!), expanded mass transit, and energy sources like biomass, wind, solar, tidal and hydro. Unfortunately, all of these sources have environmental impacts of their own, and some are "low quality" in the sense that the power intensity is low, requiring extensive investment in land and equipment. There are many opportunities for people with good ideas to help here. Google alternative energy and find many interesting sites.

2.  you will prolly have more success with the adults.  Adolescents are aweful, but in working with them, you need to come through the back door.  Like, I will find out what a certain kid likes, ex. Eminem, and have it playing as they come in for their first session.  Most of em are like, "Wow you like that music."  and that's the back door.  Also, teenagers don't wanna know that they are being counseled, so you need to be "under the hood" when talking with them.  Some sort of activity that they are interested in.

3.  Study contempory adlerian therapy for children.  

4.  In my experience, 99% of the time it is the child's aweful past with someone or their parents who are really messed up.  I never met a problem kid with Beaver Cleaver parents.

5. stay patient..kids like these can drive you bonkers at times...to keep yourself sane...keep saying that this kid is sick or his family is sick...stay with em'...they need me...you find in time that these same kids will tell you as they have told me with tears in their eyes, "You're not gonna leave me too are u. Good Luck and take care.

Title: disposable camera?
Question: how it works, material used
Answer: The dictionary calls a "camera" a chamber and when the court meet "in camera" it is in the judge's chamber (away from the public and jury).  Therefore a photographer's camera is nothing more than a darkened chamber that protects film from light exposure until you click and open an aperture to let the light (and view) in through the focusing lens just long enough to expose the film.  Usually you can wind the film to obtain a series of exposures on a roll of film.  The most expensive cameras often take only one picture but with remarkable clarity because of the very costly lenses and timing mechanisms.  These might be used to shoot the gatefold in color for a men's magazine, etc.  A disposable camera performs the same function for snapshots using barely adequate but inexpensive lenses with little control of the camera and photo possible.  Because it is mass-produced and not designed to be refilled with fresh film, it is cheap enough to use once and throw away (as in disposable).

Title: Does anyone have a successful instant credit program idea?
Question: I am a manager for a retail chain that allows customers to open up lines of credit instantly at our checkouts. We have entered a dull season (the time between Labor Day and Back To School) and our instant credit performance is slipping, even though we have offered a high-ticket item as incentive. Does anyone have any successful ideas for employee motivation, pitch ideas or anything that can help raise our numbers back to goal?
Answer: You never want to give away gifts in exchange for a credit sign-up - as a rule of thumb, financial programs are poorly sold when a financial incentive is provided up front.  Your target audience are individuals who desire to make a purchase but may be hesitating due to lack of funds and credit.  So go to the highest priced items in your store, and have signs that say, "$100 for this TV, but if you sign up for a credit card today, you only pay $12 per month in payments" etc.  Market the card next to your highest price gifts to drive adoption of the credit program. When the jungles died and separated, what would become man developed a locking knee joint. This enabled them to walk much farther (and endurance run) to cover more ground and obtain more resources, putting them at a distinct advantage to other primates. If you don't believe me, try walking around without locking your knee, it's hard and taxing.\n\nThis adaptation allowed for the development of many other things that we've come to love: our large heads and brains (when we were strictly bipedal, we free up our hands for projects, and this favors big brains), short rib cage (for flexibility), and big butts (something has to give you balance when you don't have a tail).\n\nThis climate change occurred when New Guinea moved in the way of a prominent current that brought warm, moist water to east Africa. Title: Another scuba question, this time about the cylinder valve.?
Question: Those of you who read scuba questions regularly, know that I'm a newbie diver, and I'm hooked. I'm trying to learn all I can topside, so I read quite a bit. 
I was never taught that the cylinder valve should be turned back 1/4 turn or a short way... in fact, in my confined water dives and the others that I've done since certification, I've never done that; I've just opened the valve.
My b/f says you should turn the valve back a bit, I've read it should be turned back in a tips booklet published by Scuba Diving magazine, yet on the Scuba Diving website, it says that the valve, once opened, should be turned back a bit or NOT AT ALL.
What is the correct procedure?
Thanks!
Answer: Open it fully (not hard) and back off 1/4 to 1/2 half turn. No more or you may cause turbulence in the 1 st stage (heat it doesn't need) and potentially causing condensation in there. Not a good thing for the reg and definitely bad news if you're diving a normal reg and even an environmental, in freezing conditions. It can also cause a possible a supply issue at depth, when you need it most. Leaving it fully open, could cause the valve to stick, making detaching the 1 st stage a vexing experience to say the least.
 It is part of the course, you may have just missed it. I've seen Instructors whip through that part mumbling.

Edit: I disagree with Don on the fully open part regarding overheads etc. So NOT true nor taught in any wreck course or technical diving course. You ARE taught to know your manifold without the need to think. If indeed you do start to turn it the wrong way, the little it has been shut is an immediate indicator. Also, when it's backed off just that little bit from open full, it has NO impact on supply or smoothness of flow to the 1st stage.

 Edit: Yup, ask your buddies, they'll agree. As for the fella that answered last...well I guess he's never seen one occur nor read even the OW manual from PADI ( I dug it out, it's in there.). It DOES happen. Just like that outdoor tap that you opened too far and need a wrench to close.
 Due to the amount of dive related questions that are popping up, this evening during a social at the local pub, I asked a pal of mine that owns a 5 star Padi to join under his shop's name. A number of years ago, this man saved my life on a wreck dive, and he's about to become a PADI Director. That's about as high as you get in that particular org as well as standing in my book. I'm not an instructor ( I got bugged again to do the course tonight for free), hence my reluctance to put the word of "god" into some of my answers here. Mine is strictly advice and experience.
 He can. Hopefully he'll join.

Question: wat is a good sceince fair project idea?
Answer: I won  the Regional Championship for this one and a trip to Canada, it was called Copy Cat. What you do is take cards with different color combinations on them and show them to students ranging from kinder-garden to the 12th asking them which color combination is their favorite. The first case is where you do it individually and then as a collective class. You should find that the younger children will stand by their first choices even during a group decision. As the children get older they are more prone to follow the choices of their peers until the later years where individuality take hold once again and they start to diversify. I used pie charts and percentages to display alot of the information and also split up the classes into males and females for a follow up experiment. Its been many many years since I did it but I'm sure the results will fascinate the judges. Good Luck!

Question: give me details in starting a new export business and the requirements to start it?
Answer: You should first find a competitive productive activity (manufacturing or natural resources) in your location and then try to establish a relationship with the providers, this activity may be, for example, artcrafts.  then you have to visit craftman in your location and show interest in buying their products.

International clients are highly demanding, so you must carefully consider build a poll of providers that guarrantee you: quality, quantities and reliability.

Once you have selected the provider then you have the first half (but the most difficult is to come)  now you have to build trust in potential buyers abroad of the product you selected to export.

In my experience I founded very useful the help of my country embassy in other countries, as well as this I highly recommend you to build an online (and printed) catalog. You should be extra careful with details in those marketing materials, NO typos, no false statements, try to be as accurate as possible and, of course, try to have those materials in at least two languages. Also be ready with quotation templates and check the payment method best suits you. again trust is important in this regard.

In this stage you may find in statistics about export of your country (given in any Economy Ministery website) about top foreign countries that most likely buy the kind of products you choose to sell from your location, keep it simple but be persistent as it takes a lot of work to get the first order, however, once you start, yopu will be in one of the most lucratives activities of the world and prosper you, as well as your family.

As you don´t give further details in your question I assume that you are starting from scratch, so, don´t worry, try to strenght relations with your friends and family, and the friends of your friends and the family of your family, try to find in your personal network those fellows that may help you connect the chain (find the best provider or find the first client) in any case prepare your selling speech for each case and be ready to show leadership and motivation, remember that doing business is a human activity and in involves inter-personal relationship skills.

Also, remember to keep it simple, export follows the same principle of local selling, you buy as cheap as possible and sell as expensive as possible (your profit will be the difference)

buy cheap and sell expensive (but be fair in both sides)

Don´t kill the gold eggs chicken by trying to get all the eggs at once, keep you baance and try to not be so greedy.

Beware of international scams!.  In my website www.somosnegocios.com  I have many recommendations for doing business internationally, check in the FAQ section, If you have further questions feel free to ask me.

Best regards

Alejandro

His song is being written by his ways;
for each, but once, may don life’s wings and fly.
One man controls the volume of his days.

A breast so warm, a collar blue, may raise
him to his feet—but soon will wave thereby,
his song is being written by his ways.

His peers and he conquer the world, a phase
where sight becomes so bright, it blinds the eye.
This man controls the volume of his days.

The vice of life so twists as youth betrays—
his well of youth, so opportune, near dry.
His song is being written by his ways.

With desperate fire, his gray will sets to blaze:
too weak, too late, too dry to catch the eye,
this man controlled the volume of his days.

And now, in silent soil from silent days,
cry fools that thought no scythe would make them lie.

One man controls the volume of his days.

Title: What about better brake lights?
Question: measure brake cylinder pressure | to microcontroller

standard brake light set ensures standard reliable function

additionally

"tracer" brake light set 1-4

tracer light set strobes when anti-lock function enabled

or

brake cylinder 'over'pressure
Answer: In automitive engineering it is often hard to define "better" especially in a competitive litigeous world.  As you mention, your brake lights are meant to alert the driver behind you.  Without a considerable amount of education, I think it would be difficult to train other drivers to interpret what you are doing with your brakes.  When accidents are caused it may become the burdon of the person braking to prove they did not cause confusion in a law suit.  If everyone has the same brakes, there should be less (lawyer caused?) confusion.  For example, some drivers merely tap on their brakes to alert a tailgater to back off.  The brake light comes on with little or no real braking action.

However, there is no reason that novel methods of making brake lights more practicable, efficient and reliable should not be adopted.  Modern cars now are required to have brake lights in the rear window as well as at the tail lights; because that places them more at eye level.  Progress is slow but sure.  There is in engineering what is called the "coke bottle" effect.  For many many years Coke used the same small green coke bottle, because it worked!  If you change something that "works" you may solve one proble but create three new problems.  That said Coke did move on to use clear glass Coke bottles and bottles in larger sizes and plastic too.  Each advance may have given them new production headaches while on the learning curve.  I'd encourage you to pursue your novel ideas; but always search for the adverse effects.  Good luck.

The Bath of Athena 

By Callimachus

Note: The "Bath of Athena" describes how Teiresias went blind after seeing the Goddess Athena naked but was given prophetic vision. The speaker of this hymn is an officiant at the Temple of Athena of Argos, preparing for the ritual bath of the statue of the Goddess. 

All you that are companions of the Bath of Athena, come forth, come forth! I heard just now the snorting of her holy horses, and the Goddess is ready to go. Hurry you now, O fair-haired daughters of Pelasgus, hurry! Never did Athena wash her mighty arms before she drove the dust from the flanks of her horses - not even when, her armor all defiled with filth, she returned from the war with the lawless Giants; but far first she loosed from the car her horses’ necks, and in the springs of Oceanus washed the flecks of sweat, and from their mouths that champed the bit: cleansed the clotted foam. 

O come, daughters of Achaea, but bring not myrrh nor alabaster (I hear the whir of her axle now!); bring not, you companions of the Bath, for Pallas myrrh, nor alabaster (for Athena does not wear perfume), neither bring you a mirror: she is sure of her beauty. Not even when Paris judged the contest on mount Ida; the great Goddess looked not into orichale nor into the transparent flow of the river Simois, nor did Hera. But Aphrodite took the shining bronze and often altered and again altered the same lock. While my Goddess, after running a two-hundred stade course, like the twin Spartan stars on the banks of Eurotas, then did her simple annointments: oil from her olive tree, applied with skill; and the blush, my dear maidens, that ran up her body was like the color of the morning rose or the seed of the pomegranate. Therefore now also bring you only this masculine virgin oil, with which Castor and with which Hercules anoint themselves. And bring her a comb all of gold, that she may comb her hair, when she had anointed her glossy tresses. 

Come forth, Athena! This company pleasing to your heart awaits you, the maiden daughters of Acestor’s mighty sons. Athena, come, the ancient rite is begun, the shield of Diomedes is carried to Inachus, an Argive rite taught by Eumedes, your beloved priest who on a time, when he knew that the people were plotting and planning his death, fled with your holy image to the hill called Creion - and set you in rocks, you, O Goddess, on the rugged rocks, whose name is now the Pallatid rocks. 

Come forth, Athena, Sacker of Cities, Athena, helmeted in gold, Athena, who rejoices in the crash of horses and shields. Come. Today, the city will drink from small springs and fountains, but not from the river; girls will dip pitchers in Physadeia today, maidens will bear water from Amymone's pool where the daughter of Danaus lives. For, mingling his waters with gold and with flowers, the river Inachus will flow from his pastoral hills, bringing fair water for the Bath of Pallas Athena. But beware, O Pelasgian river, brim your eyes to the Queen: the man who sees Pallas, Keeper of Cities, naked, shall look on Argos for this the last time. Come, Lady Athena, and meanwhile I shall say somewhat unto these. The story is not mine but told by others. 

There was a time in Thebes, my dears, Athena loved a nymph, loved her to distraction, loved her more than any other, the mother of Teiresias, Chariclo by name, and was never apart from her. When Athena drove her horses towards ancient Thespiae or towards Coroneia or to Haliartus, riding through the farmlands of the Boeotians - or toward Coroneia where her grove is heavy with incense, and her altars lie close to the river Curalius - often did the Goddess set the nymph upon her car and there was no dalliance of nymphs nor sweet ordering of dance, where Chariclo did not lead.
